sanskrit: bṛhaspate prathamaṁ vāco agraṁ yat prairata nāmadheyaṁ dadhānāḥ | yad eṣāṁ śreṣṭhaṁ yad aripram āsīt preṇā tad eṣāṁ nihitaṁ guhāviḥ ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, that first beginning of Vāc — when they set forth, giving names — that which was their best, that which was pure and free from blemish: it was hidden in them and revealed through love.

sanskrit: saktum iva titaunā punanto yatra dhīrā manasā vācam akrata | atrā sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni jānate bhadraiṣāṁ lakṣmīr nihitādhi vāci ||
english: Sifting the flour as with a sieve — therein the wise ones fashioned Speech with their mind. Friends discerned their friendships there; good fortune was sealed within their speech.

sanskrit: yajñena vācaḥ padavīyam āyan tām anv avindann ṛṣiṣu praviṣṭām | tām ābhṛtyā vy adadhuḥ purutrā tāṁ sapta rebhā abhi saṁ navante ||
english: By sacrifice they traced the track of Speech; they found her entered and dwelling among the seers. Fetching her, they distributed her in many places; the seven chanters glorify her together.

sanskrit: uta tvaḥ paśyan na dadarśa vācam uta tvaḥ śṛṇvan na śṛṇoty enām | uto tvasmai tanvaṁ vi sasre jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsāḥ ||
english: Yet one man, though seeing, does not see Speech; another, though hearing, does not hear her. But to this one she reveals her body, as a loving wife, beautifully robed, reveals herself to her husband.

sanskrit: uta tvaṁ sakhye sthirapītam āhur nainaṁ hinvanty api vājiṇeṣu | adhenva carati māyayaiṣa vācaṁ śuśruvāṁ aphalām apuṣpām ||
english: They say of one who is a friend: he has drunk the draft of friendship, yet even in the contests they do not incite him. He wanders on fruitlessly, through delusion — having heard Speech that is barren and flowerless.

sanskrit: yas tityāja sacividaṁ sakhāyaṁ na tasya vācy api bhāgo asti | yad īṁ śṛṇoty alakaṁ śṛṇoti nahi praveda sukṛtasya panthām ||
english: He who has abandoned a friend who knows his way — he has no share whatsoever in Speech. What he hears, he hears in vain; he has not found the path to what is well done.

sanskrit: akṣaṇvantaḥ karṇavantaḥ sakhāyo manojaveṣv asamā babhūvuḥ | ādaghnāsa upakakṣāsa u tve hradā iva snātvā u tve dadṛśre ||
english: Friends with eyes, friends with ears — they proved unequal in the contests of the mind. Some reached up to the shoulder, others to the chest; as those who have bathed in a lake, they have been seen there.

sanskrit: hṛdā taṣṭeṣu manaso javeṣu yad brāhmaṇāḥ saṁyajante sakhāyaḥ | atrāha tvaṁ vi jahur vedyābhir ohabrahmāṇo vi caranty u tve ||
english: When the brāhmaṇas as friends celebrate together, in the flashes of thought fashioned within the heart — there some have fallen away from the knowable; the would-be-Brahman wanderers go about still among them.

sanskrit: ime ye nārvāṅ na paraś caranti na brāhmaṇāso na sutakarāsaḥ | ta ete vācam abhipadya pāpayā sirīs tantraṁ tanvate aprajajñayaḥ ||
english: These who move neither hither nor beyond, who are neither brāhmaṇas nor pressers of Soma — they, having come to Speech by a sinful path, spin the thread of weavers, unknowingly.

sanskrit: sarve nandanti yaśasāgatena sabhāsāhena sakhyā sakhāyaḥ | kilbiṣaspṛt pituṣaṇir hy eṣām araṁ hito bhavati vājinaya ||
english: All friends rejoice in the one who has come gloriously, who overcomes assemblies; he who removes guilt and procures food is well fitted for the contest — for such is their helper.

sanskrit: ṛcāṁ tvaḥ poṣam āste pupuṣvān gāyatraṁ tvo gāyati śakvarīṣu | brahmā tvo vadati jātavidyāṁ yajñasya mātrāṁ vi mimīta u tvaḥ ||
english: One dwells in the prosperity of the hymns having nourished it; another sings the gāyatra verse in the śakvarī chants; one proclaims the knowledge of Brahman that was born; yet another measures out the measure of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: devānāṁ nu vayaṁ jānā pra vocāma vipanyayā | uktheṣu śasyamāneṣu yaḥ paśyād uttare yuge ||
english: Let us now proclaim with praise the generations of the gods, so that one may behold them in a later age when the hymns are being recited.

sanskrit: brahmaṇas patir etā saṁ karmāra ivādhamat | devānām pūrvye yuge 'sataḥ sad ajāyata ||
english: Brahmaṇaspati blew these together as a smith blows the bellows: in the earliest age of the gods, Being was born from Non-Being.

sanskrit: devānāṁ yuge prathame 'sataḥ sad ajāyata | tad āśā anv ajāyanta tad uttānapadaḥ pari ||
english: In the first age of the gods, Being was born from Non-Being. After that the regions were born; and after that, from Uttānapāda.

sanskrit: bhūr jajña uttānapado bhuva āśā ajāyanta | aditer dakṣo ajāyata dakṣād v aditiḥ pari ||
english: Earth was born from Uttānapāda; from the earth the quarters were born. From Aditi, Dakṣa was born; and from Dakṣa, Aditi.

sanskrit: aditir hy ajaniṣṭa dakṣa yā duhitā tava | tāṁ devā anv ajāyanta bhadrā amṛtabandhavaḥ ||
english: For Aditi was born, O Dakṣa — she who is your daughter. After her were born the gods, the blessed ones, who have immortality as their bond.

sanskrit: yad devā adaḥ salile susaṁrabdhā atiṣṭhata | atrā vo nṛtyatām iva tīvro reṇur apāyata ||
english: When the gods, all banding together, stood fast in the ocean — then a piercing dust, as though from those who dance, arose from them.

sanskrit: yad devā yatayo yathā bhuvanāny apinvata | atrā samudra ā gūḍham ā sūryam ajabhartana ||
english: When, like ascetics striving in discipline, the gods swelled the worlds — then from the ocean they drew forth the hidden sun.

sanskrit: aṣṭau putrāso aditer ye jātās tanvaḥ pari | devāṁ upa prait saptabhiḥ parā mārtāṇḍam āsyat ||
english: Aditi had eight sons born from her body. She approached the gods with seven; but Mārtāṇḍa she cast away.

sanskrit: saptabhiḥ putrair aditir upa prait pūrvyaṁ yugam | prajāyai mṛtyave tvat punar mārtāṇḍam ābharat ||
english: With seven sons Aditi went forth to meet the earlier age. But for birth and death she brought Mārtāṇḍa back again.

sanskrit: janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāya mandra ojiṣṭho bahulābhimānaḥ | avardhan indram maruto cid atra mātā yad vīraṁ dadhanaḍ dhaniṣṭhā ||
english: He was born mighty for strength, for swiftness — gladdening, most vigorous, of great self-pride. Even the Maruts increased Indra when his most bounteous mother bore the hero.

sanskrit: druho niṣattā pṛśanī cid evaiḥ purū śaṁsena vāvṛdhuṣ ṭa indram | abhīvṛteva tā mahāpadena dhvāntāt pratpitvād ud aranta garbhāḥ ||
english: The dappled ones, fixed in the midst of trickery, increased Indra with manifold praise. Like ones enclosed, those embryos arose from darkness and from pre-dawn with a great stride.

sanskrit: ṛṣvā te pādā pra yaj jigāsy avardhan vājā uta ye cid atra | tvam indra sālāvṛkān sahasram āsan dadhiṣe aśvinā vavṛtyāḥ ||
english: Mighty are your feet when you go striding forward; the prizes grew — even those that were here. You, Indra, subdued a thousand wolves in their lairs; you would have turned the Aśvins to your side.

sanskrit: samanā tūrṇir upa yāsi yajñam ā nāsatyā sakhyāya vakṣi | vasāvyām indra dhārayaḥ sahasrāśvinā śūra dadatur maghāni ||
english: With equal swiftness you come to the sacrifice; you bring the Nāsatyas to friendship. You hold the prayer of treasure, O Indra; the heroic Aśvins gave their bounties.

sanskrit: mandamāna ṛtād adhi prajāyai sakhibhir indra iṣirebhir artham | ābhir hi māyā upa dasyum āgān mihaḥ pra tamrā avapat tamāṁsi ||
english: Rejoicing from the law for the sake of progeny, Indra with his swift friends aimed at the goal. By these powers he came upon the Dasyu; he scattered the dark ones like drops of dew, dispersing the darknesses.

sanskrit: sanāmānā cid dhvasayo ny asmā avāhann indra uṣaso yathānaḥ | ṛṣvair agacchaḥ sakhibhir nikāmaiḥ sākam pratiṣṭhā hṛdyā jaghantha ||
english: Even though of the same name, the smiters fell before him; Indra drove them back as Dawns drive away the night. You came with your noble willing friends; and together, standing firm, you smote what was dear to the heart.

sanskrit: tvaṁ jaghantha nucim makhasyuṁ dāsaṁ kṛṇvāna ṛṣaye vimāyam | tvaṁ cakartha manave syonān patho devatrāñjaṁ seva yānān ||
english: You slew Namuci who lusted for sacrifice, making the Dasyu powerless before the seer. You made smooth paths for Manu, like roads well-anointed leading to the gods.

sanskrit: tvam etāni papriṣe vi nāmeśāna indra dadhiṣe gabhastau | anu tvā devāḥ śavasā madanty uparibudhnān vaninas cakartha ||
english: You filled all these with your fame; you hold them, ruling, Indra, in your hand. The gods exult with you in your strength; you made trees spring up from their roots above.

sanskrit: cakaṁ yad asyāpsv ā niṣattam uto tad asmai madhv ic cacchadyāt | pṛthivyām atiṣitaṁ yad ūdhaḥ payo goṣv adadhā oṣadhīṣu ||
english: The wheel that is fixed in the waters — may it pour sweet honey for him. The udder spread upon the earth — the milk you have placed in the cows, in the plants.

sanskrit: aśvād iyāyeti yad vadanty ojaso jātam uta manya enam | manyar iyāya harmyeṣu tasthau yataḥ prajajña indro asya veda ||
english: When they say 'He came from the horse' — and yet I think him born of strength; he came from fury and stood in the houses. The source from which Indra was born, that he himself knows.

sanskrit: vayaḥ suparṇā upa sedur indraṁ priyamedhā ṛṣayo nādhamānāḥ | apa dhvāntam ūrṇuhi pūrdhi cakṣur mumuṅghy asmān nidhayeva baddhān ||
english: The fair-winged birds — the seers Priyamedhas — alighted upon Indra, calling upon him. Roll away the darkness, fill up our sight; release us like treasures that have been bound.

sanskrit: vasūnāṁ vā carkṛṣa iyakṣan dhiyā vā yajñair vā rodasyor | arvanto vā ye rayimantaḥ sātau vanuṁ vā ye suśruṇaṁ suśruto dhuḥ ||
english: Whether one has worshipped among the Vasus by thought or sacrifices of the two worlds — or those whose swift steeds are rich with spoils in battle, or those who have given renown to the well-renowned Vaṇu.

sanskrit: hava eṣām asuro nakṣata dyāṁ śravasyatā manasā niṁsata kṣām | cakṣāṇā yatra suvitāya devā dyaur na vārebhiḥ kṛṇavanta svaiḥ ||
english: The call of these reaches the Asura in the sky; with fame-seeking mind they touch the earth. Beholding where the gods would make good fortune, as Heaven with its own clouds.

sanskrit: iyam eṣām amṛtānāṁ gīḥ sarvatātā ye kṛpaṇanta ratnam | dhiyaṁ ca yajñaṁ ca sādhhantas te no dhāntu vasavyam asāmi ||
english: This song of the immortals — in its entirety — for those who yearn for the jewel; perfecting thought and sacrifice, may they grant us unceasing wealth.

sanskrit: ā tat ta indrāyavaḥ panantābhi ya ūrvaṁ gomantaṁ titṛtsān | sakṛtsvaṁ ye puruputrāṁ mahīṁ sahasradhārāṁ bṛhatīṁ dudhukṣan ||
english: These sons of Indra praised that act — those who would reach the cow-rich pen. Those who milked the great, mighty one, with many sons, with a thousand streams.

sanskrit: śacīva indram avase kṛṇudhvam anānataṁ damayantaṁ pṛtanyūn | ṛbhukṣaṇaṁ maghavānaṁ suvṛktim bhartā yo vajraṁ naryam purukṣuḥ ||
english: By power make Indra ready for our help — the unbowed one who subdues his foes; the Ṛbhukṣin, the bounteous one, of beautiful praise, the bearer of the manly bolt, rich in nourishment.

sanskrit: yad vāvāna purutamam purāṣāḻ ā vṛtrahendro nāmāny aprāḥ | aceti prāsahas patis tuviṣmān yad īm uśmasi kartave karat tat ||
english: What Indra, the all-conquering, the slayer of Vṛtra, has desired most — he has filled up his names. The mighty lord of prevailing strength has been perceived; may he do what we desire to be done.

sanskrit: pra su va āpo mahimānam uttamaṁ kārur vocāti sadane vivasvatāḥ | pra sapta-sapta tredhā hi cakramuḥ pra sṛtvarīṇām ati sindhur ojasā ||
english: The bard shall proclaim your highest greatness, O Waters, in the house of Vivasvat. Seven by seven they have moved in three ways; the Sindhu surpasses the swiftly flowing rivers in power.

sanskrit: pra te 'radad varuṇo yātave pathaḥ sindho yad vājāṁ abhy adravas tvam | bhūmyā adhi pravatā yāsi sānunā yad eṣām agraṁ jagatām irajyasi ||
english: Varuṇa dug out the paths for you to run, O Sindhu, when you charged toward the prizes. You go over the earth upon a sloping back; when you move at the head of these, the moving ones.

sanskrit: divi svano yatate bhūmyor upary anantaṁ śuṣmam ud iyarti bhānunā | abhrād iva pra stanayanti vṛṣṭayaḥ sindhu yad eti vṛṣabho na roruval ||
english: Your roar stretches up above the earth to heaven; you raise up boundless vigor with your brightness. As the rains thunder forth from the cloud, so the Sindhu bellows as it goes, like a bull.

sanskrit: abhi tvā sindho śiśum in na mātaro vāśrā arṣanti payaseva dhenavaḥ | rājeva yudhvā nayasi tvam it sicau yad āsām agraṁ pravatām inakṣasi ||
english: They rush toward you, O Sindhu, like lowing mothers to their calf, like milch cows with their milk. As a king going to battle leads his forces, so you move at the forefront of the rushing streams.

sanskrit: imam me gaṅge yamune sarasvati śutudri stomaṁ sacatā paruṣṇy ā | asikniyā marudvṛdhe vitastayārjīkīye śṛṇuhy ā suṣomayā ||
english: O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī — come together with my hymn! O Paruṣṇī, Asiknī, Marudvṛdhā, Vitastā, Ārjīkīyā — hear it! O Suṣomā!

sanskrit: tṛṣṭāmayā prathamaṁ yātave sajūḥ susartvā rasayā śvetyā tyā | tvaṁ sindho kubhayā gomatīṁ krumum mehtnā sarathaṁ yābhir īyase ||
english: First with the Tṛṣṭāmā you go united; joined with the Rasā and the white Śvetī. You, O Sindhu, travel in the same chariot with the Kubhā, the Gomatī, the Krumu, the Mehatnu.

sanskrit: ṛjīty enī ruśatī mahitvā pari jrayāṁsi bharate rajāṁsi | adabdhā sindhur apasām apastamāśvā na citrā vapuṣīva darśatā ||
english: Rushing straight, white, mighty — it bears the realms around the courses. The Sindhu, undeceived, best of workers among rivers — like a beautiful mare with a wondrous body to behold.

sanskrit: svaśvā sindhuḥ surathā suvāsā hiraṇyayī sukṛtā vājinīvatī | ūrṇāvatī yuvatiḥ sīlamāvaty utādhi vaste subhagā madhuvṛdham ||
english: The Sindhu is rich in good horses, in good chariots, in fine garments; golden, well-formed, rich in prizes. Woolen, youthful, endowed with gifts — the fortunate one wears the garment of honey-growth.

sanskrit: sukhaṁ rathaṁ yuyuje sindhur aśvinaṁ tena vājaṁ saniṣad asmin ājau | mahān hy asya mahimā panasyate 'dabdhasya svayaśaso virapśinaḥ ||
english: The Sindhu has yoked an easy, horse-drawn chariot; with it she shall win the prize in this contest. Great indeed is the greatness to be praised of this inviolable, self-glorious, all-pervading one.

sanskrit: ā va ṛñjasa ūrjāṁ vyuṣṭiṣv indraṁ maruto rodasī anaktana | ubhe yathā no ahanī sacābhuvā sadaḥ-sado varivasya ta udbhidā ||
english: At the breaking of the strengths I reach you; anoint Indra and the Maruts with the two worlds. May both the days attend upon us together, seat by seat opening outward to give us room.

sanskrit: tad u śreṣṭhaṁ savanaṁ sunota nātyo na hastayato adriḥ sotari | vidad dhy aryo abhibhūti pauṁsyam maho rāye cit tarute yad arvataḥ ||
english: Press that best Soma-pressing; the pressing-stone is not to be touched lightly by the presser as a horse by the hand. For a noble man who finds manly power that overcomes — he wins even great wealth when he conquers the chariot.

sanskrit: tad id dhy asya savanaṁ viver apo yathā purā manave gātum aśret | goarṇasi tvāṣṭre aśvanirṇiji prem adhvareṣv adhvarāṁ aśiśrayuḥ ||
english: That is indeed his pressing's opening flood, as once it found a way for Manu. They have delighted in the Tvāṣṭra Soma-pressing — in the cow-colored, horse-stripping rite — in the sacrifices, the skilled sacrificers.

sanskrit: apa hata rakṣaso bhaṅgurāvataḥ skabhāyata nirṛtiṁ sedhata amatim | ā no rayiṁ sarvavīraṁ sunotana devāvyam bharata ślokaṁ adrayaḥ ||
english: Drive away the Rākṣasas, the evildoers; prop up Nirṛti, drive away ill-will. Press out for us all-heroic wealth; O press-stones, carry the divine-seeking praise-song.

sanskrit: divaś cid ā vo 'mavattarebhyo vibhvanā cid āśvāpastarebhyaḥ | vāyoś cid ā somarabhastarebhyo agneś cid arca pitukṛttarebhyaḥ ||
english: More powerful even than those from heaven; broader even than the all-pervading; swifter in the Soma-ladle even than Vāyu; sing of those who prepare food more perfectly than Agni.

sanskrit: bhurantu no yaśasaḥ sotv andhasur grāvāṇo vācā divitā divitmatā | naro yatra duhate kāmyaṁ madhv āghoṣayanto abhito mithastura ||
english: May they — the press-stones, glorious and inspired by inspired Speech — press out the Soma for our glory. Where the men milk the desirable sweetness, calling out together, pressing against each other.

sanskrit: sunvanti somaṁ rathirāso adrayo nir asya rasaṁ gaviṣo duhanti te | duhanti ūdhar upasecanāya kaṁ naro havyā na marjayanta āsabhiḥ ||
english: The chariot-borne stones press the Soma; they milk out the juice of it for the cow-seeking ones. They milk the udder to fill the vessels; the men purify the oblations with their mouths.

sanskrit: ete naraḥ svapaso abhūtana ya indrāya sunutha somaṁ adrayaḥ | vāmaṁ-vāmaṁ vo divyāya dhāmne vasu-vasu vaḥ pārthivāya sunvate ||
english: You men have become excellent craftsmen, you O press-stones who press Soma for Indra. Gift upon gift in your divine abode; wealth upon wealth to you who press upon the earthly.

sanskrit: abhrapruṣo na vācā pruṣā vasu haviṣmanto na yajñā vijānuṣaḥ | sumārutaṁ na brahmāṇam arhase gaṇam astoṣy eṣāṁ na śobhase ||
english: As cloud-drops sprinkle wealth with speech, as knowledgeable sacrifices with oblations — you who deserve a brāhmaṇa-hymn like that of the Maruts' troop: I have praised the host of them; you shine with them.

sanskrit: śriye maryāso añjīṁr akṛṇvata sumārutaṁ na pūrvīr ati kṣapaḥ | divas putrāsa etā na yetira ādityāsas te akrā na vāvṛdhuḥ ||
english: The young men adorned themselves with bright ornaments for glory, like those of the Maruts beyond the many nights. These sons of Heaven have not grown old; these Ādityas have grown great like eagles.

sanskrit: pra ye divaḥ pṛthivyā na barhaṇā tmanā ririce abhrān na sūryaḥ | pājasavanto na vīrāḥ panasyavo riśādasor na maryā abhidyavaḥ ||
english: They who, by their own greatness, have surpassed heaven and earth as the sun surpasses the clouds; vigorous as heroes worthy of praise, devouring their enemies, young men desiring the sky.

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṁ budhne apāṁ na yāmani vithyuryati na mahī śratharyati | viśvapsur yajño arvāg ayaṁ su vaḥ prayasvanto na satrāca ā gata ||
english: At your foundations, as in the flow of waters, the great earth does not totter, does not slip. This all-nourishing sacrifice is here toward you; come hither, like those pressing forward together.

sanskrit: yūyaṁ dhūrṣu prayujo na raśmibhir jyotiṣmanto na bhāsā vyuṣṭiṣu | śyenāso na svayaśaso riśādasaḥ pravāso na prasitāsaḥ paripruṣaḥ ||
english: You, harnessed in the shafts with reins as drivers, luminous with your brilliance at the dawning; like self-glorying eagles devouring enemies, like travelers who have rushed forth, sprinkling everywhere.

sanskrit: pra yad vahadhve marutaḥ parākād yūyam mahaḥ saṁvaraṇasya vasvaḥ | vidānāso vasavo rādhyasyārāc cid dveṣaḥ sanutarr yuyota ||
english: When you carry yourselves forward from afar, O Maruts, lords of the great treasure-store — knowing the wealth of blessings, O Vasus, drive far away all enmity, even from a distance.

sanskrit: ya udṛci yajñe adhvareṣṭhā marudbhyo na mānuṣo dadāśat | revat sa vayo dadhate suvīraṁ sa devānām api gopīthe astu ||
english: He who has offered up in sacrifice what stands in the place of the ceremony, offering to the Maruts as a man should — may he enjoy splendid nourishment with good heroes; may he be in the protection of the gods.

sanskrit: te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmā ādityena nāmnā śambhaviṣṭhāḥ | te no avantu rathatūr manīṣām mahaś ca yāmann adhvare cakānāḥ ||
english: For they are worthy of sacrifice in sacrifices, sheltering ones, most beneficent by the name of Āditya. May they protect us, swift as chariots in thought, delighting in the great journey and the ceremony.

sanskrit: viprāso na manmabhiḥ svādhyo devāvyo na yajñaiḥ svapnaṣaḥ | rājāno na citrāḥ susaṁdṛśaḥ kṣitīnāṁ na maryā arepasaḥ ||
english: Like inspired sages with their hymns, self-meditating; like the god-seeking with their sacrifices, well-awake; like brilliant kings fair to behold; like guiltless young men among the peoples.

sanskrit: agnir na ye bhrājasā rukmavakṣaso vātāso na svayujaḥ sadyaūtayaḥ | prajñātāro na jyeṣṭhāḥ sunītayaḥ suśarmāṇo na somā ṛtaṁ yate ||
english: Like Agni with his blazing splendor, gold-breasted; like the winds, self-yoked, bringing help in a single day; like the elders who know well, of good guidance; like the Soma-draughts bestowing shelter for one who goes the right way.

sanskrit: vātāso na ye dhunayo jigatnavo agnīnāṁ na jihvā virokiṇaḥ | varmaṇvanto na yodhāḥ śimīvantaḥ pitṝṇāṁ na śaṁsāḥ surātayaḥ ||
english: Like roaring winds they move and hasten; like the tongues of fires, shining out; like armored warriors, energetic; like the praises of the Ancestors, those of liberal gifts.

sanskrit: rathānāṁ na ye arāḥ sanābhayo jigīvāṁso na śūrā abhidyavaḥ | vareyavo na maryā ghṛtapruṣo abhisvartāro arkaṁ na suṣṭubhaḥ ||
english: Like the spokes of chariots, sharing one nave; like conquering heroes desiring the sky; like worthy young men sprinkling the oblation, singing forth like those of excellent praise.

sanskrit: aśvāso na ye jyeṣṭhāsa āśavo diddhiṣavo na rathyaḥ sudānavaḥ | āpo na nimnair udabhir jigatnavo viśvarūpā aṅgiraso na sāmabhiḥ ||
english: Like the eldest, the swift horses, like the charioteers who desire, of liberal gifts; like waters rushing on with downward and with upward floods; all-formed, like the Aṅgirases with their Sāman chants.

sanskrit: grāvāṇo na sūraya sindhumātara ādardirāso adrayo na viśvahā | śiśūlā na krīḍayaḥ sumātaro mahāgrāmo na yāmann uta tviṣā ||
english: Like the press-stones, the enlightened ones, whose mother is the Sindhu, always crushing; like rocks that shatter at all times; like playful young ones of good mothers; like a great host in their march and their blazing.

sanskrit: uṣasāṁ na ketavo dhvaraśriyaḥ śubhaṁyavo nāñjibhir vy aśvitan | sindhavo na yayiyo bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ parāvato na yojanāni mamire ||
english: Like the banners of the Dawns, beautiful at the ceremony, adorned with bright ornaments, they shone; like the swift rivers with flashing spears, they measured out the distances as from far away.

sanskrit: subhāgān no devāḥ kṛṇutā suranān asmān stotṝn maruto vāvṛdhānāḥ | adhi stotrasya sakhyasya gāta sanād dhi vo ratnadheyāni santi ||
english: O gods, make us fortunate, of good treasure — us, the praisers; O Maruts, who have increased; go forth upon the praise and upon the friendship — for from of old your jewel-gifts are set aside for us.

sanskrit: apaśyam asya mahato mahitvam amartyasya martyāsu vikṣu | nānā hanū vibhṛte sam bharete asInvatī bapsatī bhūry attaḥ ||
english: I beheld the greatness of this great Immortal one among the mortal peoples. The two jaws — separated and yet brought together — the insatiate eater devours abundantly.

sanskrit: guhā śiro nihitam ṛdhag akṣī asInvann atti jihvayā vanāni | atrāṇy asmai padbhiḥ sam bharanty uttānahastā namasādhi vikṣu ||
english: His head hidden in the cave, his two eyes apart — the insatiate one devours the forests with his tongue. The foods are carried to him with feet; those with upraised hands bow down in worship before the peoples.

sanskrit: pra mātuḥ prataraṁ guhyam icchan kumāro na vīrudhaḥ sarpad urvīḥ | sasaṁ na pakvaṁ avidad śucantaṁ ririhvāṁsaṁ ripa upasthe antaḥ ||
english: Seeking the deeper secret of the mother, he crept over the broad ways like a child among plants. Blazing, he found the ripe grain within; licking, the trickster was in the mother's lap.

sanskrit: tad vām ṛtaṁ rodasī pra pravīmi jāyamāno mātarā garbho atti | nāhaṁ devasya martyaś ciketa āgnir aṅga vicetāḥ sa pracetāḥ ||
english: This truth I declare to you both, O Heaven and Earth: the embryo devours the mothers at birth. I, mortal, have not fully understood the god — but Agni himself is the far-seer, the wise one.

sanskrit: yo asmā annaṁ tṛṣv āadadhāty ājyair ghṛtair juhoti puṣyati | tasmai sahasram akṣabhir vi cakṣe agne viśvataḥ pratyaṅṇ asi tvam ||
english: He who brings food and oblation eagerly to him, who pours ghee upon him and flourishes — for him, Agni, you look out with a thousand eyes; you face all ways toward him.

sanskrit: kiṁ deveṣu tyaja enaś cakartha agne pṛcchāmi nu tvām avidvān | akrīḍan krīḍan harir attave 'dan vi parvaśaś cakarta gām ivāsiḥ ||
english: What forsaking sin have you committed among the gods, O Agni? — I ask you now as one who does not know. Playing and not playing, the tawny one to eat — eating, he cut joint by joint like a sword through a cow.

sanskrit: viṣūco aśvān yuyuje vanejā ṛjītibhī raśanābhir gṛbhītān | cakṣade mitro vasubhiḥ sujātaḥ sam ānṛdhe parvabhir vāvṛdhānaḥ ||
english: The forest-born one has yoked his swift horses in different directions, grasped with reins on both sides. Mitra, well-born, looks on with the Vasus; growing with his joints, he has swelled together.

sanskrit: agniḥ saptiṁ vājambharaṁ dadāty agnir vīraṁ śrutyaṁ karrmaniḥṣṭhām | agnī rodasī vi carat samañjann agnir nārīṁ vīrakukṣim puraṁdhim ||
english: Agni gives the prize-bringing seven-horsed (team); Agni gives a famous hero, firm in action. Agni moves through the two worlds, uniting them; Agni gives the woman of heroic womb, rich in understanding.

sanskrit: agner apnasaḥ samid astu bhadrā agnir mahī rodasī ā viveśa | agnir ekaṁ codayat samatsv agnir vṛtrāṇi dayate purūṇi ||
english: May the kindling of Agni's work be auspicious; Agni has entered the great two worlds. Agni impelled the one in battles; Agni splits asunder the many Vṛtras.

sanskrit: agnir ha tyaṁ jarataḥ karṇam āvāgnir adbhyo nir adahaj jarūtham | agnir atriṁ gharma uruṣyad antar agnir nṛmedham prajayā sṛjat sam ||
english: Agni protected the ear of the old man; Agni burned up the Jarūtha from the waters. Agni saved Atri within the burning heat; Agni released Nṛmedha together with his offspring.

sanskrit: agnir dād draviṇaṁ vīrapeśā agnir ṛṣiṁ yaḥ sahasrā sanoti | agnir divi havyam ā tatānā agner dhāmāni vibhṛtā purutrā ||
english: Agni gives wealth shaped with heroes; Agni gives the seer who wins thousands. Agni has spread the oblation in heaven; the stations of Agni are carried in many places.

sanskrit: agnim ukthair ṛṣayo vi hvayante agniṁ naro yāmani bādhitāsaḥ ||agniṁ vayo antarikṣe patanto agniḥ sahasrā pari yāti gonām ||
english: The seers invoke Agni with their hymns; men pressed in need invoke Agni on their journey. Birds flying in mid-air invoke Agni; Agni moves around the thousands of cattle.

sanskrit: agniṁ viśa īḷate mānuṣīr yā agnim manuṣo nahuṣo vi jātāḥ | agnir gāndharvīm pathyām ṛtasyā agner gavyūtir ghṛta ā niṣattā ||
english: The human peoples invoke Agni; those of Manu and Nahuṣa born everywhere invoke Agni. Agni holds the Gāndharvī path of the law; the pasture of Agni is established in the ghee.

sanskrit: agnaye brahma ṛbhavastutakṣur agnim mahām avocāmā suvṛktim | agne prāva jaritāraṁ yaviṣṭhāgne mahi draviṇam ā yajasvā ||
english: The Ṛbhus fashioned a prayer for Agni; we have proclaimed great Agni with beautiful praise. O Agni, most youthful, protect the singer; O Agni, win for us great wealth by sacrifice.
